items.title: Tencent releases full Hunyuan Hy4: 770B-parameter MoE, 1M-token context, first Hy-series model with vision and Computer Use; open weights 'coming days'
items.summary: Tencent announced the full release of Hunyuan Hy4 on November 4, 2026, upgrading the August preview to its production flagship. It is a 770-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model (49B active in the preview; the full-release active count is not individually disclosed) with a 1-million-token context window. Hy4 is the first Hy-series model to add vision, and the first to add Computer Use — the capability to execute multi-step tasks by combining command-line and graphical-interface actions, in the same category as Anthropic's Claude Computer Use and ByteDance's Doubao-Vision Agent. Tencent published its own benchmark comparisons: on a Tencent-run working-agent evaluation GPT-5.6 Sol scored 80.6, Claude Opus 5 scored 77.8, and Hy4 preview scored 77.1; Tencent also claims Hy4 ties Claude Opus 5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 at 85.4 and surpasses Qwen 3.8 Max and GPT-5.6 Sol on Toolathlon-Verified. These numbers are vendor-reported and have not been independently reproduced — BenchLM's cross-model aggregator notes most direct Hy4-vs-Claude comparisons are still inconclusive on agentic work, and Artificial Analysis has not yet indexed Hy4 in its intelligence index. Hy4 is live on Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, Yuanbao, and WeChat Work, plus OpenRouter and OpenCode, with a 50% launch discount through December 31, 2026; the preview tier is listed at approximately $0.75 per million input and $2.25 per million output tokens. Hallucination rate is reported dropped from the August preview (reports vary between a drop from 15.76% to 5.45% and a drop from 12.95% to 7.2% depending on source). **Overnight update (Nov 5):** approximately 24 hours after the Nov 4 announcement, the promised open weights had not yet appeared on Tencent's Hugging Face organization — tencent/Hy3-preview remains the latest public Tencent large-model checkpoint. The community is already preparing for the drop: a third-party contributor (0xTank) has set up an NVFP4-W4A16-MTP quantization slot on Hugging Face pointing at Hy4-preview, which is the pattern you typically see 24–48 hours ahead of an open-weights release. One secondary analysis also disputes third-party inference availability — OrcaRouter says Tencent has not actually opened the model to third-party inference platforms yet despite the Nov 4 announcement listing OpenRouter and OpenCode, so the OpenRouter 'tencent/hy4-preview' endpoint should be verified before coding against it.
items.why_it_matters: There are three threads worth pulling out of this release and the first 24 hours after it. First: the Chinese frontier open-weights trajectory. Hy4 is the first Tencent model to ship vision and Computer Use, which puts Tencent on roughly the same feature line as Anthropic (Claude Computer Use, late 2024), OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Sol with agent actions), and Google (Gemini with Computer Use) — and if the 'open weights in the coming days' commitment holds, it will land at a 770B MoE scale under open license, which is larger than the current open-weight frontier (Meta Muse Spark Open at 816B and DeepSeek V4.x). The pattern through 2026 has been that Chinese labs ship open-weight versions of frontier capabilities 2–5 months after US closed releases, and Hy4 is the next data point on that curve. The emerging second thread — now that we're a day into the release — is that this timing is already slipping past 24 hours with no weights on Tencent's Hugging Face org, which is a mild but measurable deviation from the 'coming days' framing; it also makes the community-run NVFP4 quantization slot that appeared on Hugging Face in the same window a notable pre-positioning signal for the ecosystem around open frontier models. Second: Computer Use is the capability worth understanding architecturally. Rather than tool-calling a fixed set of APIs, the model takes screenshots, reasons over pixel locations, and emits mouse-and-keyboard actions — which means it can drive *any* desktop app the way a person would, not only ones with explicit integrations. For Gabe's Python stack this is the most relevant Tier-1 ecosystem shift of the quarter: the pattern is pure Python (PyAutoGUI-style action loops, screenshot capture with mss or Pillow, a vision-language model in the middle), and the primary skill to develop against it is designing a simple action schema and a verification loop that catches the model misclicking. Third: the specific Tencent-published numbers (77.1 working-agent, 85.4 Terminal-Bench 2.1 'tied with Opus 5') should still be treated as directional 24 hours in — Artificial Analysis has not yet indexed Hy4, no independent OSWorld-Verified number exists, and BenchLM's cross-model aggregator continues to flag most Hy4-vs-Claude comparisons as inconclusive. The durable numbers to watch over the next days are the open-weight release itself (if it ships at Apache-compatible terms it changes what's locally runnable) and any independent OSWorld-Verified score (Claude Opus 4.8 sits at 83.4; a comparable independent Hy4 number would be a much harder data point than the Tencent-internal eval).
items.why_it_matters_brief: First Chinese 770B MoE with vision and Computer Use — 24 hours in, the promised open weights still haven't dropped on Hugging Face, and no independent benchmarks have replaced Tencent's own numbers yet.

items.title: Apple opens Siri AI to all third-party apps via iOS 27.3 developer preview — any app can now add custom actions through App Intents, with new 'Skills' and Spotlight semantic index extensions
items.summary: On November 3, 2026, Apple published a developer-news post ('Siri AI is now open to all developers') and shipped the first iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3 developer betas. The release opens the Siri AI developer preview to every Apple developer — any app can now expose its content and actions to Siri AI through App Intents, with no new entitlement required. Users can make natural-language requests like 'check my delivery' or 'book that reservation,' and Siri AI carries them out via the app. The preview introduces two additional capabilities: Skills, which let a developer teach Siri AI to combine several actions into one multi-step experience for complex requests, and Spotlight semantic index support, which lets Siri surface any entity in the index, not just those matching an existing schema. A companion Siri Evaluations framework (beta from version 27.3) lets developers script conversations and measure how Siri responds. Apple also opened its first wave of Apple Intelligence Group Labs sessions for November 4–5 to help developers integrate. Apps can't ship Siri AI integrations to end users yet — App Store submission for third-party Siri AI integrations opens in spring 2027, and iOS 27.3 itself is expected to ship to users in December 2026. Availability is limited: English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish; Apple Intelligence-enabled device required; currently unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS (tied to Apple's ongoing Digital Markets Act posture, consistent with the broader Apple Intelligence rollout pattern that has kept core features out of the EU since mid-2024); unavailable to users under 13. Server-side Apple Intelligence features (including Siri AI) have daily usage limits, with expanded paid access planned. **Overnight update (Nov 5):** no substantive hands-on developer reviews of the Skills composition or Spotlight semantic index capabilities had surfaced in the first 24 hours — the preview is sufficiently new that only Apple's own documentation plus early forum notes are circulating. One early-beta report on the Apple Developer Forums (thread 832602) describes a developer whose App Intents are registered and work correctly in Shortcuts, yet Siri AI still returns 'I can't do that' for the matching conversational query; this is a typical day-one beta observation about the Siri intent-routing layer rather than the App Intents framework itself, and is useful context for anyone planning to prototype against the preview this week.
items.why_it_matters: This is the first time Apple has let any third-party app wire itself into a conversational AI assistant at the OS level on iPhone, iPad, and Mac — comparable in architectural shape to Google Assistant's App Actions (2019) but five years late, and arriving with actual LLM-class natural-language understanding rather than template matching. The interesting technical pattern is App Intents: Apple's existing on-device action surface originally built for Shortcuts, now acting as the glue layer for a cloud/on-device hybrid LLM. If you've ever written a Shortcut, the shape of the API will be familiar — you declare intents (named actions with typed parameters and natural-language phrasing hints) and Siri AI picks the right one from context. The new 'Skills' concept is the piece worth reading carefully: a Skill lets a developer compose several App Intents into a multi-step workflow that Siri AI treats as a single request, which is what every agentic-assistant project in 2026 has been reinventing inside a chat window. Apple is standardizing that pattern at the OS layer. For Gabe's HTML/CSS/Python stack: the direct comparison is to writing a Python tool-calling loop for a Claude or ChatGPT agent, except that on iOS the schema is declared in Swift annotations on a struct, not in a JSON tool definition. The portable idea — declare actions with typed parameters and natural-language descriptions, let the LLM pick the one that matches intent — is the same pattern, and watching how Apple's constraints (privacy, on-device fallback, parameter resolution UI) shape the API is a readable case study in productionizing agentic UX. The 24-hour-later read (Nov 5) hasn't changed the shape of this story but adds one practical note: early-beta Siri intent routing still mis-fires on registered App Intents, per developer-forum reports, which is exactly where a brittle agentic-assistant layer tends to break — the routing layer between natural-language query and typed action is the hard problem, and a public Apple beta surfacing that mis-route behavior inside the first week is useful early signal. The long date gap is also still the news: a developer preview in November 2026, apps shipping in spring 2027, means Apple has still not actually delivered the third-party AI integration demoed at WWDC 2024 — the two-and-a-half-year lag is concretely measurable, and the spring 2027 ship date is itself a soft commitment. The EU exclusion continues to put a hard floor on how global this ecosystem can be and is worth watching as a DMA / Apple Intelligence regulatory data point.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Any iOS app can now wire itself into Siri AI through App Intents and a new 'Skills' composition layer — early-beta reports already show Siri's intent-routing mis-firing on registered App Intents, the exact failure mode where agentic-assistant layers tend to break first.
